summary: Jefferson County, WA: two Webb Mountain lookouts; the summit building was destroyed in 1966, sources conflict on the build sequence, and a 1955 benchmark and outhouse remain.

facts.design: Two-story enclosed cabin with garage topped by an L-4 cab (FFLOS, Firelookout.com); WashingtonLookouts describes a 16-foot round timber tower with a 14x14 R-6 plan cab
facts.status_note: Summit lookout destroyed in 1966 per Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; FFLOS dates the removal of its sidehill cabin to 1966. Little remains at the summit; the lower site has one foundation with a post and two vertical timbers per WillhiteWeb.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service per FFLOS; Washington State Division of Forestry/DNR per Firelookout.com

visit.drive_up: Summit: gravel road described as mostly good, about 2 miles. Lower site: about 0.2 miles from a parking area at the clear-cut edge, reached by gravel road 2510
visit.trail_note: Final mile of summit road has become a bushwhack; at the lower site, climb the hillside from the parking area

events.note: Sidehill building begun about 1934 (FFLOS, Firelookout.com); WashingtonLookouts dates a 16-foot round timber tower on the Hoodsport district to 1934
July 1, 1936 document judged the lower site a poor place and recommended re-establishing the lookout further back on the ridge
Summit building built or moved there around 1937 or 1938; WillhiteWeb offers the lower-cab-moved-up idea as a working theory
Aircraft Warning Service station activated March 16, 1942 (Olympia Filter Center); WillhiteWeb calls it a year-round AWS station
Summit lookout destroyed per Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; FFLOS dates the removal of its sidehill cabin to 1966
Registered February 20, 2011; nominated by Irene Potter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says a 2-story cabin on a sidehill was built 1934 by the Washington Division of Forestry; Firelookout.com says a 10-foot pole L-4 tower on a sidehill came first (about 1934) and the 2-story cabin was on the summit by 1939; WillhiteWeb says the summit building was built or moved there around 1937-38; WashingtonLookouts gives 1934 for a 16-foot tower on the upper page. Unresolved; the story presents the accounts without choosing one.

Sources describe the summit building as a 2-story slant-walled cabin topped by an L-4 cab (FFLOS, Firelookout.com) or as a 16-foot timber tower with a 14x14 R-6 plan cab (WashingtonLookouts). The brief says R-6. The R-6 label is attributed to a structural inventory on WashingtonLookouts; a web search returned a summary saying R-6 dates from 1953, but no fetched page confirmed that. Unresolved.
FFLOS dates the removal of its sidehill 2-story cabin to 1966; Firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say the summit building was destroyed in 1966. Same year; the building attribution differs (see built).
FFLOS: U.S. Forest Service administers; Firelookout.com: Washington State Division of Forestry/DNR. Unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Build sequence unresolved across four accounts (see resolved_conflicts), so confidence is low. The R-6 label appears only on WashingtonLookouts, which cites a structural inventory; a search summary claimed R-6 dates from 1953, which was not verified by a fetched page, so do not repeat that claim without checking. The 'three_story' label in the brief is consistent with WillhiteWeb text but is not a research key. Brief coordinates not checked. The brief record calls the lower site 'upper' only in the title; the summit is the site the brief record describes.
